{{nihongo|'''Ibaraki Shrine'''|茨木神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|ar|إباراكي (أوساكا)|ca|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ce|Ибараки (гӀала)|ceb|Ibaraki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Ibaraki|eo|Ibaraki (urbo)|es|Ibaraki (Osaka)|et|Ibaraki|fa|ایباراکی، اوساکا|fi|Ibaraki (Osaka)|fr|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ga|Ibaraki|gl|Ibaraki|hy|Իբարակի|it|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ja|茨木市|ka|იბარაკი (ქალაქი)|ko|이바라키시|mzn|ایباراکی، اوساکا|nl|Ibaraki (Osaka)|no|Ibaraki (Osaka)|pl|Ibaraki|pt|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ro|Ibaraki, Osaka|ru|Ибараки (город)|sh|Ibaraki|simple|Ibaraki, Osaka|sr|Ибараки|sv|Ibaraki, Osaka|tg|Ибараки|th|อิบารากิ (จังหวัดโอซากะ)|tl|Ibaraki, Osaka|tr|Ibaraki, Osaka|tt|Ибараки (шәһәр)|uk|Ібаракі (Осака)|ur|ایباراکی، اوساکا|vi|Ibaraki, Ōsaka|war|Ibaraki, Osaka|wuu|茨木市|zh|茨木市|zh_classical|茨木市|zh_min_nan|Ibaraki-chhī|zh_yue|茨木|qid=Q502403}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. Within the precincts, the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine also stands. {{nihongo|'''Ibaraki Shrine'''|茨木神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* Principal deity — {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Takehaya-Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
* Associate deities — {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Honda Wake-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the founding dates to {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191}} 2 ({{ill|807|Q30016|qid=Q30016}}), when {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|bn|সাকানোউয়ে নো তামারামারো|ca|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|de|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|el|Σακανόουε νο Ταμουραμάρο|es|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|eu|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|fa|ساکانواوئه نو تامورامارو|fr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|it|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ja|坂上田村麻呂|ko|사카노우에노 다무라마로|pl|Tamuramaro Sakanoue|pt|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ru|Саканоуэ-но Тамурамаро|simple|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|sl|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|tr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|uk|Саканоуе но Тамурамаро|vi|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|zh|坂上田村麻呂|zh_classical|坂上田村麻呂|zh_min_nan|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|qid=Q941979}} established the village of Ibarakiri no Sato (the origin of the place name "Ibaraki," said to be near present-day Miyamoto-chō); at that time, Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine—now the rear shrine (okumiya)—was founded. At that time, the shrine was located in what is now Miyamoto-chō, Ibaraki. The name Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine also appears in the "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}." It is variously said that the shrine was moved to its present location when {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|Q382234|qid=Q382234}} built {{ill|Ibaraki Castle|Q11617856|qid=Q11617856}}, or that it moved in the late {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. When it moved to the current site, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo}} and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Ōkami}} were jointly enshrined in the main hall with Ame-no-Iwatowake Ōkami, and {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman Ōkami}} was enshrined in a separate building. The shrine received the reverence of successive castle lords ever since.

During the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, {{ill|Nakagawa Kiyohide|Q6960145|qid=Q6960145}}, lord of Ibaraki Castle, was a devout patron of the shrine. He erected a prohibition notice strictly forbidding lawless behavior against the shrine, and in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 8 ({{ill|1580|Q6712|qid=Q6712}}) he donated 13 koku of shrine lands.

The lord of {{ill|Takatsuki Castle|Q11670758|qid=Q11670758}}, {{ill|Justo Takayama|Q749873|qid=Q749873}}, protected {{ill|Christianity|Q5043|qid=Q5043}} while destroying neighboring temples and shrines. At that time, {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} issued an order that shrines enshrining {{ill|Amaterasu|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}}, Kasuga Ōkami ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}), Hachiman Ōkami ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Honda Wake-no-Mikoto}}), and {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}} (Susanoo)—Nobunaga's own {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}}—must not be burned. Therefore, this shrine concealed the name Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine and styled itself "Gozu Tennō-sha" to escape destruction by Ukon (see also [https://web.archive.org/web/20020525192200/homepage.mac.com/ryomasuda/Saigoku/history/KamiGami/Goz3.html]).

In {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245}} 8 ({{ill|1622|Q6815|qid=Q6815}}), a new main hall was built to enshrine Gozu Tennō (Susanoo), Kasuga Ōkami (Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto), and Hachiman Ōkami (Honda Wake-no-Mikoto), and the former Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine became the rear shrine (okumiya).

{{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, but when parishioners began petitioning for shrine-rank authorization for Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine as well, in {{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}} (Meiji 12) Ame-no-Iwatowake Shrine was also ranked as a gōsha. This made it a nationally rare shrine with two gōsha within a single precinct. The following year, {{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}} (Meiji 13), a heiden and haiden were constructed, but they were replaced with new buildings in {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 4).

== Precinct ==
* Honden (main hall) — built in {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245}} 8 ({{ill|1622|Q6815|qid=Q6815}}). Restored in {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 4).
* Heiden — rebuilt in 2022 (Reiwa 4). The previous building was demolished due to deterioration.
* Haiden (worship hall) — rebuilt in 2022 (Reiwa 4). The previous building was demolished due to deterioration.
* Plum garden — as one of the {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} Imperial Enthronement projects, approximately 50 red and white plum trees were planted in {{ill|1991|Q2062|qid=Q2062}} (Heisei 3).
* Kuroi no Shimizu — together with Akai no Shimizu and Aoi no Shimizu, it has been one of the three famous springs of {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimashimo District}} since ancient times. It is said to have been used for {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}'s tea ceremony as well.
* Visitor rest house (Muharaki-sha) — built in February {{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}} (Heisei 23).
* East gate — when {{ill|Ibaraki Castle|Q11617856|qid=Q11617856}} was abandoned in Genna 3 ({{ill|1617|Q6798|qid=Q6798}}), its karamete-mon (rear gate) was received and relocated here.
* Assembly hall — built in 1991 (Heisei 3). The first floor houses the shrine office and mikoshi storehouse; the second floor is an assembly room.
* Ceremonial hall — built in {{ill|1966|Q2649|qid=Q2649}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 41). The first floor is the saikan (purification hall); the second floor is a wedding hall.

== Auxiliary shrines ==

Associate deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|Q462803|qid=Q462803|lt=Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyokuni-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977|lt=Tōshō-shin}}. The original main shrine of this site and an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Shikinaisha}}. == Major rites ==
* January 1: Saitan-sai
* January 9–11: Tōka Ebisu Festival
* February 11: Kigen-sai
* April 8: Ningyō Hōshō-sai (doll burning ceremony)
* April 18: Kinen-sai
* June 30: Ōharae
* July 13–14: Natsu-matsuri (summer festival)
* October 10: Reitaisai (annual grand festival)
* November 23: Niiname-sai
* December 31: Ōharae
